questions.scenario: Transfer events are keyed by transfer reference. A consumer must see TransferReserved before TransferCleared for the same transfer.
questions.question: Why does this work?
options: Kafka orders every topic globally
Records with the same key go to the same partition, and order is guaranteed within a partition
Consumers sort records by timestamp
The broker delays later events until earlier ones are acknowledged
questions.explanation: The producer hashes the key to pick a partition; order holds only within a partition, so same key means same order.

questions.scenario: A topic has 3 partitions. The fraud service runs 4 instances in the same consumer group.
questions.question: What happens?
options: Each record is processed four times
Kafka adds a fourth partition automatically
Three instances each get a partition; the fourth sits idle
The group fails to start
questions.explanation: Within a group each partition goes to one consumer, so consumers beyond the partition count are idle.

questions.scenario: Notifications and fraud both need every transfer event.
questions.question: How should they consume transfer-events?
options: With different group ids, so each group gets every record
With the same group id, so the load is shared
One should read from the other's output
By deleting records once read
questions.explanation: Each group tracks its own offsets and receives all records; sharing a group id would split the events between them.

questions.scenario: A consumer commits its offset as soon as it receives a batch, then crashes half-way through processing it.
questions.question: What is the result?
options: The unprocessed records are delivered again
Kafka rolls the commit back
The records are moved to a dead-letter topic
The unprocessed records are skipped: at-most-once delivery
questions.explanation: Committing before processing loses in-flight records after a crash. Commit after processing for at-least-once.

questions.scenario: A money-events topic has replication factor 3.
questions.question: Which producer and topic settings make a confirmed record survive the loss of one broker?
options: acks=all with min.insync.replicas=2
acks=0 for speed
acks=1 with min.insync.replicas=1
Any settings: replication alone is enough
questions.explanation: acks=all waits for the in-sync replicas, and min.insync.replicas=2 refuses writes that only one broker holds.

questions.scenario: A consumer subscribes to transfer-events before it exists. The broker auto-creates it with 1 partition; another service then declares it with 3.
questions.question: What can go wrong?
options: Nothing: Kafka merges the definitions
The topic is deleted and recreated
Consumers may not notice the two new partitions for minutes, so records there wait unprocessed
Records are duplicated across partitions
questions.explanation: This is why production clusters switch auto-creation off and every service declares topics with the same partition count.

questions.scenario: Your team lead says Kafka 4 still needs a ZooKeeper cluster.
questions.question: What is accurate?
options: Only for consumer groups
Kafka 4.0 removed ZooKeeper; metadata is managed by Kafka itself with KRaft controllers
Only on Kubernetes
Only when replication factor is above 1
questions.explanation: KRaft replaced ZooKeeper; in Kafka 4 there is no ZooKeeper mode at all.

questions.scenario: Transfers needs to know whether an account has enough money before it continues.
questions.question: Should that be a Kafka event?
options: Yes, every interaction should be an event
Yes, with a reply topic for every request
No: it's a question that needs an answer now, so a synchronous call fits
No, Kafka can't carry balances
questions.explanation: Events announce facts for others to react to later; a question the caller waits on is a synchronous call.
